Good article, though it is about GMail, it could largely apply to Search as you mention.

The negative spin is that it takes something user-controlled, predictable, clear and linear and takes control away from the user, making email unpredictable, unclear and nonlinear.

The reason is that Google is in the algorithm business, using user-activity "signals" to customize and personalize the online experience and the ads that are served up as a result of those signals.

Get back to the old days of the Internet where you paid your email provider, and you'll have a better experience in the long run. Search is a bit more of an issue though... Even in the context of the article. Search by its nature has to be mediated; While mail can be sorted in chronological order, what order would it make sense to sort search results in? If the search index was just a long list of websites and their content, with no attempts at connecting websites to each other, discovering their associations, or figuring out which one you might actually have wanted, it would be a bit of a mess. For instance, if you search for "XD" are you searching for the pistol, or the stupid fucking "smiley" that kids use. I think we all expect and accept some amount of mediation in search, but we don't want anything specifically removed from our searches (censorship) nor do we want a database amassed of our search requests and browsing behavior (privacy).
